q: Do bank loans to start-ups count as priority sector lending in India?
title: Start-up loans and priority sector
short: Yes, up to ₹50 crore per start-up, with start-up as defined by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The loan sits in the category that fits the business: agriculture and allied services, MSME if the start-up meets the MSME definition, or the Others category for start-ups outside both.
audience: Start-up founders and CFOs raising bank debt, and their lenders

sections.h: Three places a start-up loan can sit
ul: Agriculture, ancillary services: loans up to ₹50 crore to start-ups engaged in agriculture and allied services (para 9.3).
MSME: loans up to ₹50 crore to start-ups that conform to the MSME definition (para 10). All bank loans to MSMEs already qualify, so Udyam registration is what the bank will check.
Others: loans up to ₹50 crore to start-ups in activities other than agriculture or MSME (para 16).

p: The Directions use the definition set by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, not a separate RBI test. Ask your bank which recognition document it wants on file, and keep it with your loan papers.

Under the notification of 21 March 2025, a micro enterprise has up to ₹2.5 crore in plant and machinery and ₹10 crore turnover, a small enterprise up to ₹25 crore and ₹100 crore, and a medium enterprise up to ₹125 crore and ₹500 crore.
A loan that counts towards a bank's priority sector target is one the bank is keen to make. It does not by itself mean a lower rate or a smaller collateral demand.

senseible: Senseible gives a climate or hardware start-up a bill-based energy and emissions record that lenders and investors can trace, without a consultant building it by hand.
